subject: MAP + evaluation timeline: hosting mode & geo lock for Acme Health
messages:
From: Lucinda Park <lucinda@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Apr 01 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff: hosting mode + regional lock for PHI workloads

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Acme is narrowing toward a production target in Q3 and we want to lock the MAP so procurement and security can align. Two immediate asks:

1) Recommendation and timeline for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for EU PHI workloads (data residency + SOC 2 evidence).
2) A mutual action plan we can give to Procurement with clear milestones and a go/no-go date.

I've attached our internal timeline spreadsheet — we can share it if useful (see attachment stub). We expect demo/poc in April and a pilot in May. Procurement also needs an estimate for monthly committed capacity and an outline of what triggers a private deployment.

Can you propose a draft MAP by Friday? Also cc'ing Karthik for technical feasibility.

Thanks,
Lucinda
Director, Cloud Ops
Acme Health

Attachments: Acme_Timeline_Q3.xlsx (stub)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Lucinda Park <lucinda@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Apr 02 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: hosting mode + regional lock for PHI workloads

Hi Lucinda — great talking through requirements. Draft MAP attached (AcmeHealth_MAP_v2.xlsx) and a short summary below.

Executive summary (short):
- Shortlist: Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (predictable capacity), Private (required only if contractually necessary for PHI).
- Recommendation: Proceed with a staged plan: Hosted Canary (eu-west-1, data plane controls) -> Dedicated for sustained traffic if latency/cost dictates -> Private only if legal requires certified on-prem/VPC KMS.
- Go/no-go date for pilot: 2027-05-10. Production gate: 2027-06-21.

Mutual Action Items (high level):
- Redwood: provide SOC2 summary, latency profile for eu-west-1, cost estimate for 3 capacity tiers (by 2027-04-05).
- Acme: confirm PHI surface and whether de-identification will be used, complete procurement intake form (by 2027-04-08).
- Joint: schedule security review and procurement sync (by 2027-04-09).

Risk notes:
- If residency constraints require physical isolation, timeline extends by ~6-8 weeks for Private onboarding.
- Dedicated provisioning lead time depends on GPU type; we recommend an initial 2-week reserved capacity window for the pilot.

I attached SOC2Summary.pdf and the MAP spreadsheet. Can you confirm the go/no-go cadence you need from procurement? If Friday works, we can lock the MAP and circulate to Legal.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Attachments: AcmeHealth_MAP_v2.xlsx (stub), SOC2Summary.pdf (stub)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Lucinda Park <lucinda@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, Apr 05 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: hosting mode + regional lock for PHI workloads

Lucinda / Kimberly — quick technical note to add to the MAP:

- Latency: If the application targets <75ms p95 for short-turn prompts, we should plan Dedicated with pinned GPU pools close to the ingestion region. Hosted can meet initial needs but may see higher variance during peak.
- KV cache & batching: We can enable prefix caching for deterministic requests in the pilot to reduce tokens and cost.
- Data residency enforcement: For eu residency, we can enforce region pinning and audit logs; however, for regulatory proof (if required), Private (VPC + customer KMS/HSM) is the option.

Suggested timeline additions (technical):
- Week of 2027-04-12: Provision eu-west-1 pilot nodes (hosted reserving burst capacity).
- Week of 2027-05-03: Canary tests (latency/throughput) with 10k requests/day simulated.
- Week of 2027-05-24: Swap to Dedicated if sustained throughput expected and latency SLOs unmet.

If Procurement needs a firm trigger for Private, recommend the clause: "Private onboarding triggered if legal requires physical isolation or encryption key custody controlled by Acme."

—Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Lucinda Park <lucinda@acmehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, Apr 06 2027 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: hosting mode + regional lock for PHI workloads

Thanks, this is helpful. A couple clarifications from Procurement and Security:

- PHI scope: We will have limited PHI in metadata fields for triage; main content will be de-identified but cannot guarantee full de-identification for first 30 days.
- Procurement asks for a firm monthly commitment estimate for Q3 and a template statement of work (SOW) and an estimated MRC for Dedicated.
- Security would like a SOC2 attestation and an initial runbook for incident response in eu region.

Our preferred path is: start Hosted canary in eu-west-1 for validation while working procurement in parallel — if legal flags PHI residency, we will request Private onboarding. Can you confirm the cost delta between Hosted pilot and Dedicated baseline (MRC) in the next 48 hours? Also, we will need a DocuSign-ready agreement by 2027-04-18 to meet internal procurement cadence.
